acquisition: The data-dependent acquisition method consisted of MS1 acquisition (R=70,000) using an MS AGC target value of 3e6, followed by up to 15 MS/MS scans (R=17,500) of the most abundant ions detected in the preceding MS scan.
labeling: Relative DHA and DHB peptide levels were quantified and compared to their non-modified peptide counterparts.
quantification: The relative level of modification was defined as the ratio of the peak area of modified peptide to the peak area of the non-modified summed with the modified peptide and multiplied by 100.
enrichment: The pellet was solubilized in 8M urea... this fraction was defined as the urea-soluble fraction (USF). The remaining pellet was suspended in water and proteins from this fraction were defined as the urea-insoluble fraction (UIF).
workflow_hints: DHA modifications on cysteine (-33.9877 Da) and serine (-18.0106 Da), and DHB modification on threonine (-18.0106 Da).

Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The study focuses on specific spontaneous degradation PTMs (DHA and DHB). While it uses solubility-based fractionation (WSF, USF, UIF) to isolate proteins, it does not use standard antibody-based enrichment for these PTMs. The quantification is performed by comparing modified vs non-modified peptide peak areas (LFQ approach).

scope: Lens tissue was manually homogenized in homogenization buffer comprised of 25 mM Tris, 150 mM NaCl, and 5 mM EDTA and centrifuged at 20,000 g for 30 minutes.
Proteins from each region and fraction (WSF-IN, WSF-ON, WSF-C, USF-IN, USF-ON, USF-C, UIF-IN, UIF-ON, and UIF-C) were quantified via a bicinchoninic acid (BCA) assay.

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The material analyzed consists of different solubility fractions (water-soluble, urea-soluble, and urea-insoluble) derived from homogenized lens tissue. While these are fractions based on solubility, they do not map to the specific organelle or subcellular compartment terms provided in the ontology context (e.g., nuclear, mitochondrial, cytosolic).
